group: Early exit based on RCODE

input.value: Message with QUESTION section only, RCODE = Rcode.FORMERR

cases.expected: Returns the original Message instance (this) without modification
cases.description: When the response RCODE is neither NOERROR nor NXDOMAIN the method should return the original message unchanged.

input.value: Message with QUESTION section only, RCODE = Rcode.NXDOMAIN

cases.expected: Continues processing (does not return early)
cases.description: NXDOMAIN is allowed, so the method proceeds to normalisation.

group: DNAME handling – multiple entries in DNAME RRset

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset with 2 records

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: If a DNAME RRset contains more than one record and throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true, the method must throw a WireParseException.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset with 2 records

cases.expected: null
cases.description: When throwOnIrrelevantRecord is false the method logs a warning and returns null for the same situation.

group: DNAME handling – query type is DNAME (no CNAME synthesis)

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = alias.example.com, type = DNAME; ANSWER contains a single‑record DNAME RRset for alias.example.com → target.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains exactly the original DNAME RRset and no synthesized CNAME
cases.description: When the query itself asks for DNAME, the method must keep the DNAME RRset and must not synthesize a CNAME.

group: DNAME handling – synthesize CNAME when appropriate

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a single‑record DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com followed by no CNAME

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains the original DNAME RRset and a synthesized CNAME RRset (www.example.com → target.com) with TTL=0
cases.description: When a DNAME is present and the query type is not DNAME, the method must add a synthesized CNAME pointing to the DNAME target.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com and a CNAME RRset for www.example.com that already matches the synthesized target

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains the DNAME RRset only (the existing CNAME is recognised as correct and not duplicated)
cases.description: If the next RRset is a CNAME that already matches the expected synthesized CNAME, the method must skip adding a new CNAME.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = ANY; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com followed by an unrelated RRset for old.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains DNAME, synthesized CNAME and the extra RRset for old.example.com (because query type is ANY)
cases.description: When the query type is ANY the method must keep additional records that have the original name after the DNAME processing loop.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com; the DNAME target is so long that Name.fromDNAME throws NameTooLongException

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown (wrapped NameTooLongException)
cases.description: If synthesising a CNAME fails due to a NameTooLongException and throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true, the method must throw a WireParseException.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com; the DNAME target is too long

cases.expected: null
cases.description: Same situation as above but with throwOnIrrelevantRecord false – the method logs a warning and returns null.

group: Irrelevant records in ANSWER section (name mismatch)

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = wanted.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains an A RRset for other.example.com

cases.expected: Message where the irrelevant RRset is omitted from the cleaned ANSWER section
cases.description: Records whose name does not match the current sname must be ignored.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = wanted.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains an A RRset for other.example.com

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: When throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true the same situation must raise a WireParseException.

group: CNAME handling – multiple CNAME RRs in one RRset

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = alias.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a CNAME RRset for alias.example.com with two CNAME records

cases.expected: Message where the CNAME RRset contains only the first CNAME record (the second removed) and sname updated to the target of the first CNAME
cases.description: When a CNAME RRset contains more than one record, the method must keep only the first and drop the rest, unless throwOnIrrelevantRecord forces an exception.

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = alias.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a CNAME RRset for alias.example.com with two CNAME records

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: If throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true the method throws a WireParseException when multiple CNAMEs are present.

group: CNAME handling – ANY query with extra records after CNAME

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = alias.example.com, type = ANY; ANSWER contains CNAME RRset for alias.example.com → target.example.com followed by an A RRset for alias.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains the CNAME RRset and also the following A RRset (preserved because query type is ANY)
cases.description: When the query type is ANY, records that appear after a CNAME with the original name must be kept.

group: Record type mismatch in ANSWER (non‑ANY query)

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = host.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains an AAAA RRset for host.example.com

cases.expected: Message where the AAAA RRset is omitted from the cleaned ANSWER section
cases.description: If the queried type is not ANY and the RRset type does not match the query, the RRset is ignored.

group: Authority section – forbidden types (switch case)

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains RRsets of type DNAME, CNAME, A, AAAA

cases.expected: Message where none of those RRsets appear in the cleaned AUTHORITY section
cases.description: The switch statement must ignore RRsets of type DNAME, CNAME, A and AAAA in the authority section.

group: Authority section – disallowed type for section

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains an RRset of type SRV (assuming isTypeAllowedInSection returns false for SRV in AUTHORITY)

cases.expected: Message where the SRV RRset is omitted from the cleaned AUTHORITY section
cases.description: If isTypeAllowedInSection returns false for a type in the authority section, the RRset must be ignored.

group: Authority NS handling – subdomain check

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = sub.example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains an NS RRset for other.com

cases.expected: Message where the NS RRset is omitted because its name is not a subdomain of the query name
cases.description: NS RRsets must be a subdomain of the current sname; otherwise they are ignored.

group: Authority NS handling – NXDOMAIN or NODATA suppression

input.value: Message with RCODE = NXDOMAIN; QUESTION name = example.com; AUTHORITY contains an NS RRset for example.com

cases.expected: Message where the NS RRset is omitted because the response is NXDOMAIN
cases.description: When the response code is NXDOMAIN, NS records in the authority section must be ignored.

input.value: Message with RCODE = NOERROR, ANSWER section empty, AUTHORITY contains an SOA RRset and an NS RRset for example.com

cases.expected: Message where the NS RRset is omitted because this is a NODATA response (SOA present and ANSWER empty)
cases.description: When the response is NOERROR, an SOA is present in authority and there is no answer, NS records must be ignored.

group: Authority NS handling – duplicate NS RRsets

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains two NS RRsets for example.com

cases.expected: Message where only the first NS RRset is kept; the second is ignored
cases.description: Only the first NS RRset is allowed; subsequent NS RRsets are ignored.

group: Successful normalisation – overall flow

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a CNAME RRset (www.example.com → alias.example.com) and an A RRset for alias.example.com; AUTHORITY contains an NS RRset for example.com; ADDITIONAL contains an A RRset for ns1.example.com

cases.expected: A new Message (cleanedMessage) whose ANSWER section contains the CNAME RRset and the A RRset (both kept), AUTHORITY contains the NS RRset, ADDITIONAL contains the original additional A RRset (because it was referenced by the NS), and header counts are updated accordingly
cases.description: A typical successful case exercising CNAME following, additional‑section handling and proper header count fixing.

group: CNAME query type – do not follow CNAME

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = alias.example.com, type = CNAME; ANSWER contains a CNAME RRset (alias.example.com → target.example.com) and an A RRset for alias.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains only the original CNAME RRset (the A RRset is omitted because the query type is CNAME and the code does not follow the CNAME). The sname is not updated, and no synthesized CNAME is added.
cases.description: When the query asks for CNAME, the normalize method must keep the CNAME RRset but must not follow it. Subsequent records with the same name are ignored because the query type is not ANY.

group: DNAME with mismatching existing CNAME – synthesize new CNAME

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = www.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains a DNAME RRset for example.com → target.com followed by a CNAME RRset (www.example.com → wrong.example.com)

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains the DNAME RRset and a synthesized CNAME RRset (www.example.com → target.com) with TTL=0. The mismatching original CNAME RRset is omitted because its target does not match the synthesized one.
cases.description: If a CNAME follows a DNAME but does not match the expected synthesized target, the method must still synthesize the correct CNAME and discard the mismatching CNAME.

group: Authority section – allowed non‑NS type and related additional record

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = mail.example.com, type = MX; AUTHORITY contains an MX RRset for example.com; ADDITIONAL contains an A RRset for mail.example.com (the MX host). Assume isTypeAllowedInSection returns true for MX in AUTHORITY.

cases.expected: Message whose AUTHORITY section contains the MX RRset and whose ADDITIONAL section contains the A RRset for the MX host (added by addAdditionalRRset). No other sections are altered.
cases.description: When an allowed type (MX) appears in the authority section, it should be kept and any additional records that are referenced by that RRset must be retained in the cleaned ADDITIONAL section.

group: Duplicate NS in AUTHORITY with throwOnIrrelevantRecord = true

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains two NS RRsets for example.com

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown (duplicate NS RRset detected and throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true)
cases.description: When a second NS RRset is encountered in the authority section, the method normally ignores it. If throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true, it must raise a WireParseException.

group: Empty ANSWER section – only AUTHORITY and ADDITIONAL processed

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; ANSWER section empty; AUTHORITY contains an NS RRset for example.com; ADDITIONAL contains an A RRset for ns1.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section is empty, AUTHORITY contains the NS RRset, ADDITIONAL contains the A RRset (added via addAdditionalRRset), and header counts reflect these sections.
cases.description: When there are no answer records, the method should still process authority and additional sections, preserving allowed records.

group: ANY query – retain all answer types regardless of query type

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = host.example.com, type = ANY; ANSWER contains an A RRset, a AAAA RRset, and a TXT RRset for host.example.com

cases.expected: Message whose ANSWER section contains the A, AAAA, and TXT RRsets (all retained because the query type is ANY).
cases.description: For an ANY query the normalize method must not filter out answer RRsets based on type.

group: Irrelevant NS in AUTHORITY with throwOnIrrelevantRecord = true

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = sub.example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains an NS RRset for other.com (not a subdomain of the query name)

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown (NS RRset is irrelevant to the query name and throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true)
cases.description: When an NS RRset in the authority section does not belong to a subdomain of the current sname, it is considered irrelevant. With throwOnIrrelevantRecord enabled, the method must raise an exception.

group: Answer section – type mismatch with throwOnIrrelevantRecord true

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = host.example.com, type = A; ANSWER contains an AAAA RRset for host.example.com

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: When the answer RRset type (AAAA) does not match the query type (A) and the query is not ANY, the method should treat the RRset as irrelevant. With throwOnIrrelevantRecord = true, logOrThrow must raise a WireParseException.

group: Authority section – forbidden types with throwOnIrrelevantRecord true

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains RRsets of type DNAME, CNAME, A and AAAA

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: The switch statement in the authority‑section loop must ignore RRsets of type DNAME, CNAME, A and AAAA. When throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true, each ignored RRset should cause a WireParseException via logOrThrow.

group: Authority section – disallowed type with throwOnIrrelevantRecord true

input.value: Message with QUESTION name = example.com, type = A; AUTHORITY contains an SRV RRset for example.com (isTypeAllowedInSection returns false for SRV in AUTHORITY)

cases.expected: WireParseException thrown
cases.description: If isTypeAllowedInSection reports that a type (e.g., SRV) is not permitted in the AUTHORITY section, logOrThrow must raise a WireParseException when throwOnIrrelevantRecord is true.
